01 GREP
ASSIGNMENT 03 / TASK 01

Log Filtering

COMPLETE

WHAT THE TASK REQUIRES

Identify failed or denied activities, extract error-related messages, perform a case-insensitive search for login failures, and display matching-record counts.

HOW THE SOLUTION WORKS

  • `grep -E` enables extended regular expressions so `FAILED|DENIED` can be matched in one command.
  • `grep -i` performs case-insensitive matching, useful for searching text such as login failures regardless of capitalization.
  • `grep -c` returns the number of matching lines instead of printing all records.
  • The error-message search includes the actual dataset wording: failed, denied, invalid, and locked.
task_01.sh // SE25UCSE019 
grep -E 'FAILED|DENIED' system_access_log.txt
grep -Ec 'FAILED|DENIED' system_access_log.txt

grep -Ei 'error|failed|denied|invalid|locked' system_access_log.txt
grep -Eic 'error|failed|denied|invalid|locked' system_access_log.txt

grep -i 'LOGIN|FAILED' system_access_log.txt
grep -ic 'LOGIN|FAILED' system_access_log.txt
OUTPUT INTERPRETATION

The filtering stage isolates the security-relevant records from the raw access log. The dataset contains 40 FAILED/DENIED records in total, and 20 of those are failed LOGIN activities. This confirms that login failures form a major portion of the security events.

02 GREP + REGEX
ASSIGNMENT 03 / TASK 02

Advanced Pattern Searching

COMPLETE

WHAT THE TASK REQUIRES

Identify IP-bearing records, search for .pdf or .csv resources, display FAILED or DENIED records, and exclude successful activities.

HOW THE SOLUTION WORKS

  • The IPv4-style regular expression searches for four numeric groups separated by periods.
  • The resource expression `\.(pdf|csv)` matches either a PDF or CSV resource path.
  • `grep -v 'SUCCESS'` inverts the match so successful activity is excluded.
  • Count mode is used to verify the number of matching records in each category.
task_02.sh // SE25UCSE019 
grep -Ec '([0-9]{1,3}\.){3}[0-9]{1,3}' system_access_log.txt
grep -Ec '\.(pdf|csv)' system_access_log.txt
grep -Ec 'FAILED|DENIED' system_access_log.txt
grep -vc 'SUCCESS' system_access_log.txt
OUTPUT INTERPRETATION

All 100 records contain an IP address. The dataset contains 38 PDF/CSV-related resource records. There are 40 FAILED/DENIED records, and excluding SUCCESS also leaves 40 records, showing that every non-success activity is represented by FAILED or DENIED status in this dataset.

PROOF OF EXECUTION

03 AWK
ASSIGNMENT 03 / TASK 03

Data Extraction

COMPLETE

WHAT THE TASK REQUIRES

Generate reports showing User ID and Name, Name and Department, User Name and IP Address, and Resource with its access status.

HOW THE SOLUTION WORKS

  • `-F'|'` tells `awk` that the log file is pipe-delimited.
  • The report selects fields directly: `$3` User ID, `$4` Name, `$6` Department, `$9` Status, `$10` IP, and `$11` Resource.
  • `printf` keeps the extracted output aligned and readable.
  • Only the required fields are displayed; the original source records remain unchanged.
task_03.sh // SE25UCSE019 
awk -F'|' '{printf "%-6s | %-10s\n",$3,$4}' system_access_log.txt
awk -F'|' '{printf "%-10s | %-5s\n",$4,$6}' system_access_log.txt
awk -F'|' '{printf "%-10s | %-15s\n",$4,$10}' system_access_log.txt
awk -F'|' '{printf "%-25s | %s\n",$11,$9}' system_access_log.txt
OUTPUT INTERPRETATION

The output demonstrates structured extraction from a raw log without manually editing the input. Each report presents only the fields relevant to the requested view, proving that `awk` can act as a lightweight reporting tool for delimited log data.

04 AWK CONDITIONS
ASSIGNMENT 03 / TASK 04

Conditional Data Analysis

COMPLETE

WHAT THE TASK REQUIRES

Display CSE users, Faculty and Researcher activities, FAILED/DENIED activity, and users who performed DELETE operations.

HOW THE SOLUTION WORKS

  • Conditions are applied directly to known fields such as department `$6`, role `$7`, action `$8`, and status `$9`.
  • Logical OR combines Faculty and Researcher activity in one report.
  • The FAILED/DENIED condition isolates security-relevant activity.
  • Filtering action `$8 == "DELETE"` identifies delete operations regardless of final status.
task_04.sh // SE25UCSE019 
awk -F'|' '$6=="CSE" {print $4,$6,$7,$8,$9}' system_access_log.txt

awk -F'|' '$7=="Faculty" || $7=="Researcher" {print $4,$6,$7,$8,$9}' system_access_log.txt

awk -F'|' '$9=="FAILED" || $9=="DENIED" {print $1,$4,$6,$8,$9}' system_access_log.txt

awk -F'|' '$8=="DELETE" {print $1,$4,$6,$8,$9}' system_access_log.txt
OUTPUT INTERPRETATION

The conditional reports prove that `awk` can filter the same dataset in several useful ways without creating intermediate files. The screenshot shows examples of CSE activity, Faculty/Researcher actions, FAILED/DENIED events, and DELETE operations in one compact analysis workflow.

05 AWK REPORT
ASSIGNMENT 03 / TASK 05

Statistical Report

COMPLETE

WHAT THE TASK REQUIRES

Generate totals for all log records, successful/failed/denied activities, unique users, and activity counts for each department.

HOW THE SOLUTION WORKS

  • A `total` counter increments for every record.
  • Status counters are incremented by checking field `$9`.
  • An associative array keyed by `$3` stores unique user IDs; counting its keys gives the unique-user total.
  • A department associative array keyed by `$6` accumulates activity totals for CSE, IT, EEE, and ECE.
task_05.sh // SE25UCSE019 
awk -F'|' '
{
    total++

    if ($9=="SUCCESS") success++
    else if ($9=="FAILED") failed++
    else if ($9=="DENIED") denied++

    users[$3]=1
    dept[$6]++
}
END {
    for (u in users)
        unique++

    print "===== STATISTICAL REPORT ====="
    print "Total log records       :", total
    print "Successful activities   :", success
    print "Failed activities       :", failed
    print "Denied activities       :", denied
    print "Unique users            :", unique
    print ""
    print "Department Activity:"
    print "CSE :", dept["CSE"]
    print "IT  :", dept["IT"]
    print "EEE :", dept["EEE"]
    print "ECE :", dept["ECE"]
}' system_access_log.txt
OUTPUT INTERPRETATION

The statistical report confirms 100 total log records: 60 SUCCESS, 30 FAILED, and 10 DENIED. The file contains 12 unique users. Department activity is distributed as CSE 42, IT 25, EEE 17, and ECE 16. These values provide a concise overview of overall system activity before deeper security analysis.

06 SED
ASSIGNMENT 03 / TASK 06

Stream Editing

COMPLETE

WHAT THE TASK REQUIRES

Convert dates from DD/MM/YYYY to YYYY-MM-DD, replace SUCCESS/FAILED/DENIED with readable labels, and remove unnecessary displayed fields where appropriate.

HOW THE SOLUTION WORKS

  • A capture-group substitution rearranges the date into ISO-style year-month-day format.
  • Status substitutions convert machine-like status words into more readable labels.
  • A field-removal expression omits the email address from the displayed stream.
  • The command edits only the output stream; it does not overwrite the source file.
task_06.sh // SE25UCSE019 
sed -E '
s#^([0-9]{2})/([0-9]{2})/([0-9]{4})#\3-\2-\1#;
s/\|SUCCESS\|/|Successful|/g;
s/\|FAILED\|/|Failed|/g;
s/\|DENIED\|/|Access Denied|/g;
s/^(([^|]*\|){4})[^|]*\|/\1/
' system_access_log.txt
OUTPUT INTERPRETATION

The transformed output is easier to read while preserving the meaning of each log entry. Dates are standardized, statuses are more human-readable, and an unnecessary field is removed from the displayed result. This demonstrates non-destructive stream editing.

07 SED / MASKING
ASSIGNMENT 03 / TASK 07

Data Masking

COMPLETE

WHAT THE TASK REQUIRES

Create a sanitized log that masks email addresses and IP addresses while preserving all other information and leaving the original dataset unchanged.

HOW THE SOLUTION WORKS

  • The email regular expression replaces complete email addresses with `[EMAIL MASKED]`.
  • The IP regular expression replaces IPv4-style values with `[IP MASKED]`.
  • Redirection writes the sanitized output into `sanitized_log.txt` instead of modifying the source.
  • `shasum` is used as an integrity check for the original input file.
task_07.sh // SE25UCSE019 
sed -E '
s/[[:alnum:]._%+-]+@[[:alnum:].-]+\.[[:alpha:]]{2,}/[EMAIL MASKED]/g;
s/([0-9]{1,3}\.){3}[0-9]{1,3}/[IP MASKED]/g
' system_access_log.txt > sanitized_log.txt

shasum system_access_log.txt
OUTPUT INTERPRETATION

The screenshot shows that email addresses and IP addresses are masked while dates, user IDs, names, roles, actions, statuses, resources, and messages remain visible. The original file checksum provides evidence that the source file was not modified during sanitization.

08 UNIX PIPELINE
ASSIGNMENT 03 / TASK 08

Combining grep, sed and awk

COMPLETE

WHAT THE TASK REQUIRES

Produce a report containing only FAILED or DENIED activity, formatted as Date | User | Department | Action | IP using a combined pipeline.

HOW THE SOLUTION WORKS

  • `grep` performs the first-stage security filter.
  • `sed` converts the date into YYYY-MM-DD format.
  • `awk` selects only the five requested report fields.
  • `printf` creates aligned columns, making the final output suitable for a concise report.
task_08.sh // SE25UCSE019 
grep -E 'FAILED|DENIED' system_access_log.txt |
sed -E 's#^([0-9]{2})/([0-9]{2})/([0-9]{4})#\3-\2-\1#' |
awk -F'|' '
BEGIN {
    printf "%-12s | %-10s | %-10s | %-8s | %-15s\n",
           "Date","User","Department","Action","IP"
    print "-------------------------------------------------------------------"
}
{
    printf "%-12s | %-10s | %-10s | %-8s | %-15s\n",
           $1,$4,$6,$8,$10
}'
OUTPUT INTERPRETATION

This task demonstrates the Unix pipeline model: each utility performs one specialized operation and passes its result to the next. The final table contains only security-relevant records and only the fields explicitly required by the assignment.

09 BASH AUTOMATION
ASSIGNMENT 03 / TASK 09

Automated Security Report

COMPLETE

WHAT THE TASK REQUIRES

Create `security_report.txt` containing total security events, users associated with FAILED/DENIED activity, the most frequent failed/denied action, relevant IP addresses, and a department summary.

HOW THE SOLUTION WORKS

  • The Bash script stores the input and output filenames in variables so the workflow is reusable.
  • FAILED/DENIED records are repeatedly filtered as the source for every security-report subsection.
  • `sort -u` removes duplicate user names and IP addresses.
  • Associative counting in `awk`, followed by numerical sorting, identifies the most frequent failed/denied action and summarizes departments.
task_09.sh // SE25UCSE019 
#!/bin/bash

LOG="system_access_log.txt"
OUT="security_report.txt"

{
    echo "Total Security-Related Events:"
    grep -Ec 'FAILED|DENIED' "$LOG"

    echo ""
    echo "Users Associated with FAILED/DENIED Activities:"
    grep -E 'FAILED|DENIED' "$LOG" |
    awk -F'|' '{print $4}' |
    sort -u

    echo ""
    echo "Most Frequently Occurring Failed/Denied Action:"
    grep -E 'FAILED|DENIED' "$LOG" |
    awk -F'|' '{count[$8]++} END {for (a in count) print a, count[a]}' |
    sort -k2,2nr |
    head -1

    echo ""
    echo "Relevant IP Addresses:"
    grep -E 'FAILED|DENIED' "$LOG" |
    awk -F'|' '{print $10}' |
    sort -u

    echo ""
    echo "Department Summary:"
    grep -E 'FAILED|DENIED' "$LOG" |
    awk -F'|' '{count[$6]++} END {for (d in count) print d, count[d]}' |
    sort
} > "$OUT"

echo "Security report generated successfully: $OUT"
OUTPUT INTERPRETATION

The automated report summarizes 40 security-related events. The affected users shown are Ananya, Diya, Ishita, Meera, Neha, and Sana. LOGIN is the most frequent failed/denied action with 20 occurrences. The department summary is CSE 14, ECE 6, EEE 13, and IT 7. The report is generated automatically into `security_report.txt`, making the analysis reproducible.

CONCLUSION.

This assignment demonstrates a complete command-line log-analysis workflow. `grep` is used for filtering and pattern matching, `awk` for structured extraction, conditions and statistics, and `sed` for stream transformation and privacy masking. The tools are then combined in a Unix pipeline and automated through Bash to generate a reusable security report without manually modifying the original dataset.
